### wasserstein-metric-and-continuity-equation

VERDICT: drift-blocked — AGS Theorem 8.3.1 supplier before wasserstein-metric-and-continuity-equation (order 2792)

The design at research/plan-machine-learning-track.md:L700 states the W₂ dynamic characterization on AC²([0,T]; P₂(Rᵈ)): existence of a Borel velocity solving the distributional continuity equation, the metric-speed bound for every admissible velocity, and equality for the minimum-norm velocity/action. The declared closure supplies measure, probability, weak-convergence, and expectation definitions, but not this substantial superposition/metric-derivative theorem. The smallest missing supplier is Ambrosio–Gigli–Savaré, *Gradient Flows*, Theorem 8.3.1 (or a complete intermediate lemma proving its Euclidean AC² contract), to place before this page (order 2792). I read the theorem’s full relevant proof, pp. 183–186: it constructs the velocity through the continuity-equation functional on the gradient closure, obtains the metric derivative estimate, and uses regularization/representation and projection to produce a minimal-norm field. The overview named by the design states the result but omits this proof. Consumers are wasserstein-gradient-flow-existence-and-stability (order 2793), including its Proposition 2.5 and Theorem 2.6 contracts, and mean-field-training-and-feature-learning (order 2794), including thm-many-particle-training-limit and thm-homogeneous-mean-field-global-minimizer-under-separation. Owner decision is needed on an authorized upstream supplier versus a full local intermediate proof; no page or pair is minted here. [AGS Theorem 8.3.1, pp. 183–186](https://www2.stat.duke.edu/~sayan/ambrosio.pdf).

I read those definitions/results and the full proof of Theorem 11.2.1, pp. 295–298; it invokes the general metric evolution theorem in AGS Chapter 4, so an import must retain the stated hypotheses. Owner authorization is required for the supplier pair/import or for carrying the full theorem as a proved intermediate result; no pair is minted here.
